title: Used AI as a coding partner — some thoughts after finishing v0.5.2
author: MasterSteak4510
selftext: Not a promo, just sharing process since this sub is about AI in gamedev. My project is a browser-based logistics tycoon, solo dev, vanilla JS. I've been using AI (mostly Claude/DeepSeek) as a coding partner for about 2 months. What worked: refactoring help, regex, CSS cleanup, catching stupid bugs, explaining my own code back to me after a break. What didn't work: anything where the AI needed to remember architectural decisions across multiple files — it kept suggesting patterns that contradicted what I'd already built. And every single visual thing — icons, truck markers, stamps, paper textures, the corkboard frame, the whole paper theme — is hand-coded SVG and CSS. Same with audio, sourced or synthesized by me. Tried AI image generation for a splash screen early on, looked fine at thumbnail size but fell apart at 100%, inconsistent lighting, fake-feeling grain. This sub's whole premise of AI-assisted gamedev actually forced me to be honest about where the line is. My take: AI is a fantastic pair programmer, a bad art director, and a genuinely terrible memory for your own project's conventions. Curious if others have similar splits. Playable thing in question, if anyone wants context on the visuals: [https://juba13.itch.io/eurasia-hauler](https://juba13.itch.io/eurasia-hauler)
